observations.text: SP, due to a non-standardized checklist flow on the Before Taxiing checks, did not execute the normal procedures described in the Flight Manual and in the SOPs in the prescribed sequence, omitting the ground frequency check before taxi and the formation check-in as briefed. The IP had to direct the remaining items and execute part of the procedure. Ground procedures were not completed without assistance. Further study of the normal procedures and of the pre-flight briefing frequency plan is required.

SP, due to lack of knowledge of the published procedure for the condition encountered, did not specify the A/C condition and did not decide its flight permissibility correctly and confidently, and moved the A/C controls before being aware of the ground crew's position. The IP interrupted the check and directed the sequence to completion. The procedure could not be completed without the IP's assistance.

SP, due to an incorrect braking and power technique as No2 in the taxi flow, did not keep standard distance from the leader during taxi, closing well inside the briefed spacing before the hold line. The interval was re-established only after the IP's verbal indications. The deviation was recognized and corrected with delay.

SP, due to distraction by a secondary cockpit task during the pre-taxi phase, did not execute the frequency checks on the ground timely and correctly according to the pre-flight briefing, and transmitted on the previous frequency. The checks were completed only after the IP's verbal prompts, and the leader's taxi call was answered late. The error was recognized and corrected with delay.

SP, due to a rushed checklist scan while cooperating with the ground crew, initially skipped one item of the Before Taxiing checks and stopped the A/C with slight oscillations at the last chance area. SP detected the omission and completed the item correctly, without the IP's intervention. Minor errors, recognized and corrected in a timely manner.

SP, due to divided attention between the ground frequency check and the taxi clearance, allowed the standard distance from the leader to open beyond the briefed spacing during the taxi turn as No2. SP recognized the developing gap and re-established the correct interval before the run-up area on his/her own initiative. Small error with timely self-correction and without the IP's intervention.

SP performed the ground procedures within the desired standards, executing all checks according to the checklist without the IP's intervention and following the specified taxi route. However, the frequency checks before taxi were initiated late on two occasions, and the standard distance from the leader as No2 required two corrections during the taxi. Marginal performance for the Training Section; consistency in the timing of the ground frequency checks and in taxi spacing discipline is expected to improve.

SP executed all checks according to the checklist, without the IP's intervention, in an impeccable and standardized manner, and specified the A/C condition and its flight permissibility correctly and confidently. As No2, SP maintained standard distance from the leader throughout the taxi, followed the specified taxi route with the ground path clear of obstacles, and stopped the A/C without oscillations. The frequency checks on the ground before taxi were executed timely and correctly, exactly as set in the pre-flight briefing. Accuracy and speed in all normal procedures were above the level desired for the Training Section. Above end of block MIF achieved.
